rejected.title: Nonfiction that tells a story
card: Some nonfiction tells true events in the way a story does. Memoir (a writer's account of their own life) and feature journalism (a long, in-depth news article) often do this.

Writers borrow fiction techniques: scene (an event shown moment by moment), dialogue, and character (a real person shown through actions and words). These help readers picture and care about what happened.
The content stays true to fact. The people, events and words are real, even though they are told with a storyteller's skill.
A nonfiction writer still chooses how to tell the truth, such as where to begin and which moments to show.
rejected.remember: Nonfiction can use story techniques to engage readers, while the facts stay true.

a.q: Which of these is an example of nonfiction that tells a story?
opts: A memoir that recreates a real childhood day as a scene
A novel about an invented detective in a made-up town
A table listing the rainfall recorded in Dubbo each month
A fantasy tale in which a talking fox rescues a village
a.why: A memoir is nonfiction, and recreating a real day as a scene uses a fiction technique while staying true to fact. The novel is tempting because it is a story, but its events are invented, so it is not nonfiction.
a.clue: Look for a real event told like a story.

b.q: A journalist writes a feature about a real bushfire. She opens with a firefighter's actions and spoken words, minute by minute, as they happened. What is the effect of this choice?
opts: It draws readers into the real events like a story
It shows the feature is fiction with invented events
It proves the writer has not chosen what to include
It replaces the facts with the writer's imagination
b.why: Showing real actions and words moment by moment uses scene and dialogue, which engage readers while the content stays factual. The claim that the feature is fiction is wrong: using story techniques does not make events invented, and these events really happened.
b.clue: Fiction techniques can be used with true events.
